title: AWS Observability and Audit: CloudWatch, CloudTrail and Config
summary: Quick revision notes on monitoring AWS with CloudWatch metrics, alarms, dashboards, Logs and Logs Insights, auditing API activity with CloudTrail management and data events and S3 trails, investigating who did what, and tracking resource configuration with AWS Config.

chapters.title: What This Handbook Covers

chapters.title: CloudWatch Metrics, Alarms and Dashboards
points: Metric = time-ordered data points identified by namespace + metric name + dimensions; each unique dimension combination is a separate metric
Default resolution: basic monitoring 5 min for EC2, detailed monitoring 1 min (paid); EC2 does NOT report memory or disk-used by default, so the CloudWatch agent is needed
Alarm states: OK, ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA; configured with statistic, period, threshold, evaluation periods and 'datapoints to alarm' (M out of N)
Treat missing data setting matters: notBreaching, breaching, ignore or missing; wrong choice leaves an alarm stuck in INSUFFICIENT_DATA or falsely firing
Alarm actions: SNS notification, EC2 stop/terminate/reboot/recover, Auto Scaling policy; test with 'aws cloudwatch set-alarm-state --alarm-name X --state-value ALARM --state-reason test'
Dashboards are global-capable and can mix metrics from multiple regions and accounts; metric math (e.g. errors / requests * 100) builds derived series

chapters.title: CloudWatch Logs, Logs Insights and Custom Metrics
points: Hierarchy: log group (retention + permissions) contains log streams (one per source instance/container) contains log events; retention defaults to Never expire, so set it to control cost
Logs reach CloudWatch via the CloudWatch agent, Lambda/ECS awslogs driver or SDK; the role needs logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents
Logs Insights query: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | stats count() by bin(5m) | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20
Metric filter turns log patterns into a metric (e.g. count of ERROR) that an alarm can watch; it only counts events ingested after the filter is created

Custom metrics via 'aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --namespace MyApp --metric-name Orders --value 1 --unit Count'; standard resolution is 1 min, high resolution is 1 sec (StorageResolution=1); embedded metric format (EMF) emits metrics from structured log lines
Logs Insights is charged per GB scanned, so narrow the time range and log groups; export to S3 for long-term archive

chapters.title: CloudTrail: Management vs Data Events and Trails to S3
points: CloudTrail records AWS API calls (console, CLI, SDK) as events; the Event history shows the last 90 days of management events for free, per region, and cannot be extended

Management events (control plane: RunInstances, CreateBucket, AttachRolePolicy) are logged by default; data events (data plane: S3 GetObject/PutObject, Lambda Invoke, DynamoDB item ops) are OFF by default, high volume and billed

A trail delivers events to an S3 bucket (and optionally CloudWatch Logs) for retention beyond 90 days; create with 'aws cloudtrail create-trail --name org-trail --s3-bucket-name my-logs --is-multi-region-trail' then 'start-logging'
The destination bucket needs a bucket policy allowing cloudtrail.amazonaws.com to s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject on AWSLogs/<account-id>/*
Enable log file validation (digest files with SHA-256 hashes) to detect tampering; use a multi-region trail and an organization trail for all accounts
Advanced event selectors scope data events to specific buckets or Lambda functions to control cost

chapters.title: Who-Did-What Investigations and AWS Config
points: Event record key fields: eventTime, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity (type, arn, principalId, sessionContext), sourceIPAddress, userAgent, requestParameters, errorCode

Investigate: look up by event name 'aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=TerminateInstances'; for older or data events, query the S3 trail with Athena
For assumed roles, userIdentity shows the role session; trace sessionContext.sourceIdentity or the original AssumeRole event to find the real human or federated user
AWS Config records resource configuration state and changes over time (configuration items/timeline) and evaluates it against Config rules for compliance, e.g. s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited
CloudTrail answers 'who made the API call', Config answers 'what did the resource look like before and after and is it compliant'; use both together
Config needs a recorder and delivery channel (S3 bucket); it is regional and bills per configuration item recorded; remediation can be automatic via SSM Automation

chapters.title: Observability and Audit Cheat Sheet
points: Metrics: namespace + name + dimensions; 5 min basic, 1 min detailed, 1 sec high resolution; memory and disk need the agent
Alarm: OK / ALARM / INSUFFICIENT_DATA; M of N datapoints; set treat-missing-data deliberately
Logs: group > stream > event; set retention; metric filter = new events only; Insights = pay per GB scanned
Commands: put-metric-data, set-alarm-state, start-query, create-trail, lookup-events
CloudTrail: management on by default, data events off; 90-day history; trail to S3 for longer; enable validation
Investigate: CloudTrail = who/when/from where; Config = what changed and compliance state
